claims.claim: AgentSkills.io is adopted by Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Strands Agents
A skill is a directory containing SKILL.md
allowed-tools: refund process_payment (space-delimited string)
frontmatter name and description
Skills load in three phases; ~50 tokens/skill, 1-5K on activation, 95-98% saving, 8 skills ~400 vs ~8,000 tokens
Activation phase happens on skill__activate; resources on skill__read_resource
Pack tools are the ceiling for tools
Prompt level baseline tools: allowed_tools: [get_order, search]
A skill's allowed-tools extend the prompt's tool set, capped at the pack's tools
Skills use the skill__ namespace alongside a2a__, workflow__, mcp__
skill__deactivate removes instructions and retracts tools
skill__activate description includes the discovery index, listing only the skills the current workflow state admits; withheld when the state admits none
Workflow state `skills: ./skills/billing` limits which skills are available; `none` disables skills; no field means all; applied on open, resume and transition
Skills organized into subdirectories: a state's directory filter admits skills at or under it; skills outside it are not available in that state
Skills auto-detected from the pack's skills section
sdk.WithSkillsDir and sdk.WithMaxActiveSkillsOption exist
Go snippet compiles against current API
The model drives activation by calling skill__activate
Link to examples/workflow-skills on GitHub main
Activation fails at the max-active limit, tracked per conversation

In rebuild mode (default) a grant changes the tools array, costing the cache and reported as tool.offer.rebuilt reason skill_grant; WithToolLoading stable keeps one array holding every grantable pack tool
A call to a tool the model may not call is refused with 'Tool <name> was not run: it is not available this turn' and does not run; decided per round
In stable tool loading mode the skill__activate index lists every skill whatever the state's filter; activating a skill the state does not admit is refused
